verdictSummary: The delta does the two things it claims. Task 1.6 gives the 2026-08-21 crash-window residual an owning task for the first time, and every structural claim in it is true at this snapshot: AUTO_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 2000, zero pagehide/visibilitychange/beforeunload/sendBeacon/keepalive hits in either named file, the PUT route 405s anything but GET/PUT/DELETE so sendBeacon is genuinely unusable, and the co-op exemption mirrors markDirtyAction exactly. The 'never read the response / never clear dirty / never advance baseVersion' discipline is not merely safe but REQUIRED by task 1.3: the cache's (instanceId, revision) key must stay at the pre-flush value so head validation replaces it with whatever the server actually committed. D13 is likewise sound, and better than it claims to know -- I verified against the in-flight P0b commit af7130e3 that NO private-payload shape change is needed for 6.2a, because replayCampaignSourceContracts already parses the captured sourceRecordBody and exposes the pre-fold market as baselineMarket. Four text-level edits are required. (1) Task 1.6 mandates a keepalive PUT and enumerates its best-effort caveats but omits the mechanism's own hard limit: the Fetch Standard caps keepalive bodies at 64 KiB. Measured on the local dev DB, real campaign rows are 3.2-20.3 KiB today, but the largest is 60% one append-shaped history field, so growth past the cap is plausible -- and over the cap the flush fails as a network error whose response the task says is never read, i.e. silently, inside a fix whose entire purpose is preventing silent loss. (2) Both D13 and 6.2a cite useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:549 for 'saveCampaign clears the armed timer and performs the write'; :549 is performSave, which does NOT clear the timer -- saveCampaignAction is :787. (3) 6.2a's offer-lookup source is ambiguous between the stored private baseline and the source row read in the command's own transaction; on the first reading the FIRST acceptance on every campaign is unsatisfiable, because the in-flight replay throws 'no-private-payload' when no prior private row exists. (4) The P-C CAS-bridge dependency that 6.2b newly creates is recorded only in the author's evidence JSON, not in the delta -- which is exactly the orphaning failure this very commit's residual-pointer correction exists to prevent. None of the four disturbs the decision, the requirements, or the task structure.

findings.detail:
EXECUTABILITY: every file, symbol and line the task names exists at the cited position, and the 'red today' premise is true -- there is no discard-time listener anywhere in the campaign-persistence layer, so the prescribed failing test (dispatch pagehide in jsdom without advancing timers, assert exactly one keepalive PUT) genuinely fails on an unmodified tree. The sendBeacon rejection is correct for the stated reason, verified at the route rather than assumed. The co-op skip is not an invention: markDirtyAction already returns before arming the timer when isCoopCampaign is true, so the flush honouring the same exemption keeps exactly one writer discipline and leaves residual (2) untouched, as the task says.

CONSISTENCY WITH 1.3 -- the 'never acknowledged' discipline is not merely safe, it is REQUIRED: after an unread flush the cached copy keeps its pre-flush (instanceId, revision) key. If the flush won the CAS, the server is now one revision ahead, the key mismatches, and 1.3's binary verdict replaces the cache with the server record -- which is the record carrying the rescued work. If the flush lost or never landed, the server record still wins and the window is lost, which the task admits as best-effort. Had the task instead cleared dirty or advanced baseVersion on the strength of firing, the cache would claim a revision it may not have earned and 1.3's 'only ever set from a record the server actually returned' would be violated. Note also that 1.3's dirty-state exemption is a SESSION fact and cannot survive a hard reload -- which is precisely why the flush is needed rather than redundant. The spec scenario 'An unread flush never claims a revision it did not earn' states this correctly.

KEEPALIVE AT REAL PAYLOAD SIZE -- the one gap. The Fetch Standard caps a keepalive request: if contentLength plus in-flight keepalive bytes exceeds 64 kibibytes the fetch returns a NETWORK ERROR (knowledge-based, not measured in session; flagged as such). Against that cap I measured the real persisted bodies on this machine: worst case 20.3 KiB, i.e. 32% of the budget, so the mechanism is viable TODAY and the task is not wrong to choose it. But the margin is one order of magnitude at best, and the composition measurement shows why that is not reassuring: the largest body is 60% recentlyAppliedOutcomes, an append-shaped history, and the body additionally carries dailyBattleAudit, salvageReports, gmInterventionEvents, timeCascadeEvents, processedBattleIds and unitCombatStates -- all unbounded in campaign length or roster size. A long-running real campaign can cross 64 KiB. When it does, the flush fails as a network error, and because the task mandates 'never read the response', nothing detects it. That is a silent failure introduced inside the fix for a silent failure, and it is the only best-effort caveat the task does not name (it names the no-pagehide-fired case and the unread-response case). REQUIRED: state the cap.

BFCACHE -- non-blocking. 'pagehide fires nowhere beforeunload does not' is the right way round (pagehide fires on unload AND on bfcache entry, so it is a superset), and preferring pagehide + visibilitychange:hidden is the standard recommendation, correctly covering the mobile case where pagehide may not fire. The absolute claim that 'registering it disqualifies the page from the back/forward cache' is overbroad: a beforeunload listener makes a page bfcache-ineligible in Firefox, but not in Chrome or Safari, where it is the unload event that does so. This is knowledge, NOT verified by any tool call in this session, and it does not change the conclusion -- so it is a wording narrowing, not a blocker.

findings.detail:
'FRESHNESS GAP, NOT STORAGE GAP' IS CORRECT AND NOW MEASURED. The admission brief recorded this as a genuine hole ('neither 6.1 nor 6.2 names a task that PERSISTS the market to the server in the first place'). D13's rebuttal is right and I can put a number on it: contractMarket is written at serializeCampaign.ts:194, read back at :264, and a real campaign row on this machine carries 2490 bytes of it. The market does have a durable source home; what it lacks is a freshness guarantee, which is exactly what 6.2a's typed not-durable refusal plus the client-side pre-command acknowledged save address. The alternative-rejected section is sound: the event form would put a full IContract inside a campaignEvent payload, which is the precise audience failure D12 exists to prevent.

NO CONFLICT WITH D12, AND -- BETTER THAN THE DELTA CLAIMS TO KNOW -- NO PAYLOAD-SHAPE CHANGE IS NEEDED FOR 6.2a. The author's own evidence records 6.1's shape as 'still inferred from D12 / tasks prose'. I checked it against the in-flight P0b commit directly. The private payload is {schemaVersion, baseline, acceptedContract: IContract, remainingMarket: ICampaignContractMarket} -- exactly the D12 shape D13 describes. More importantly, replayCampaignSourceContracts ALREADY parses the captured sourceRecordBody, pulls contractMarket out of it, rehydrates it (Money is a class, so the rehydrate is load-bearing) and exposes it as baselineMarket on the projection. So 6.2a's server half can be built against af7130e3 as it stands: no new field, no schemaVersion bump, no change to buildCampaignSourcePrivateEnvelope. That is a positive finding and it strengthens D13.

REQUIRED DISAMBIGUATION -- WHICH BASELINE. Two things follow from the same code read and both cut against the delta's current wording. (a) There is no contractMarket field on ICampaignSourceBaseline; the market is derived by parsing sourceRecordBody and is surfaced as ICampaignSourceContractProjection.baselineMarket. D13's phrase "the captured baseline's `contractMarket.offers`" names a field that does not exist, sending 6.2a's implementer looking for it. (b) More seriously, replayCampaignSourceContracts THROWS 'no-private-payload' when the stream carries no prior private row -- and a campaign that has never accepted a contract has none. Read literally as 'look the contractId up in the stored private baseline', 6.2a makes the FIRST acceptance on every campaign unsatisfiable: there is nothing to look it up in. The reading that works is the one task 6.1 actually describes -- the baseline is captured under the command's OWN prepared transaction ('Capture the baseline under the P0a prepared transaction ... exact persisted SerializedCampaign body'), so the offer read is against the source row read in that same transaction, and the captured baseline is the record of what was read. Both D13 ('a lookup by contractId in the captured baseline's contractMarket.offers') and the spec scenario ('absent from the contract market in the baseline captured from the persisted source record') are ambiguous between the two, and the losing reading is a bootstrap deadlock. This is cheap to fix in one clause and expensive to discover in implementation.

SHARED MIS-CITATION. D13 and 6.2a both anchor 'saveCampaign clears the armed timer and performs the write' at :549. That line is performSave, which does not clear any timer; saveCampaignAction at :787 is the function that does both. The behaviour described is real, only the anchor is wrong -- but this package is line-anchored throughout and the predecessor D12 review rejected a false line-anchored structural claim for the same reason.

findings.detail:
SATISFIABLE. The mismatch D13 records is real and I reproduced both halves at the cited lines. The requirement is satisfiable because it does not demand that the two trees be reconciled by a new function -- it demands they come from ONE commit, and 6.1's contract-only replay fold is the mechanism that makes that possible (the fold starts from the persisted source body, so the source record's missions and reduced market are derivable from the same committed acceptance that produced the compact ledger entry). 6.2b does assign the removal explicitly, in both the prose and a named failing-test row on campaignCommandActions.test.ts, and D13 pins sole ownership.

NO CONTRADICTION IN THE PACKAGE. The two statements that look like counterexamples -- task 1.2's 'the client is NOT rewired' and task 1.3's 'the client still MUTATES through the Zustand store' -- are dated receipts describing the state of the world at their receipt dates, not contracts that both writes may occur. The new SHALL constrains only the COMMITTED path and explicitly preserves today's single client-side write on the refused path, which is every campaign today because the flag is false and the route blocks. So the requirement is consistent with the package as written and is trivially satisfied in the current, unreachable-committed-path world.

LABELLING. Both new requirements are under the file's single '## ADDED Requirements' header, which is correct -- no canonical openspec/specs/campaign-authority capability exists for a MODIFIED marker to target. 'Unmet until 6.2b' is carried by ownership rather than by an inline label, matching how the pre-existing D12 requirement (unmet until 6.1) is handled in the same file, so this is consistent with the package's own convention rather than a lapse.

findings.detail:
TASK 1.6 IS CLEAN OF P-C, and for a principled reason rather than by luck: because the flush is never treated as an acknowledgement, it needs no mapping between the two counters at all -- it fires the existing PUT with the existing baseVersion and lets the server's CAS decide. That is the correct way to sidestep an unresolved bridge.

6.2 IS NOT CLEAN, AND THIS DELTA IS WHAT EXPOSES IT. Before this commit, 6.2 defined only the server-side command shape. 6.2b now newly asserts that the SOURCE RECORD's missions and reduced market are written from the commit, and simultaneously removes the client's local apply. Three consequences follow that the delta does not record. (1) The acknowledgement returns the original receipt revision plus the public head -- both journal-side numbers -- and a compact ICampaignAuthoritativeState that has no missions field, so the client has no way to learn the new SerializedCampaign row version, nor to refresh the full ICampaign its UI renders and its debounced PUT serialises. (2) The source-side write advances the campaigns row behind the client's back, leaving the client's cached baseVersion stale; the very next unrelated client mutation's auto-save PUT then either 409s or is refused by 6.1's sourceReplayFence. (3) The pre-existing 'Client storage is a cache, never a source' requirement covers LOAD-time validation only and does not reach this mid-session case. None of this is shippable-bug territory today -- the flag is false and the route blocks every campaign, so the committed path is unreachable -- which is exactly why it belongs in the text rather than in a build.

SHOULD THE DELTA SAY SO? Yes, and the delta's own reasoning demands it. This commit exists in part to fix a pointer that sent a reader to task 5.7 for a fix 5.7 never claimed, and it records that the gap 'had no owning task at all' for two weeks as a result. Leaving 6.2's dependency on an unresolved CAS bridge recorded ONLY in a session evidence JSON reproduces that failure mode one level down: the author knows it, the artefact does not. One sentence in 6.2 costs nothing and is symmetric with how D13 treats the acceptance-write mismatch -- recorded as an obligation rather than tolerated silently because the failure mode is silent.

The Fetch Standard caps a keepalive request body at 64 KiB (summed with in-flight keepalive bytes); above it the fetch returns a network error. Because the task also mandates never reading the response, an over-cap flush fails silently -- a silent failure inside the fix for a silent failure. nonBlockingNotes.note: 'Do NOT add `beforeunload`: it fires nowhere `pagehide` does not, and registering it disqualifies the page from the back/forward cache.' The first half is correct (pagehide is a superset: it fires on unload AND on bfcache entry).
